harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node4's HTTP service (port 8080) on node2's transit address port 80, and gave node1 a route to it. Built a dedicated transit link (node1 eth1 10.50.12.2/24 <-> node2 vtnet1/OPT1 10.50.12.1/24) and a dedicated lan-b link (node2 vtnet2/OPT2 10.50.24.1/24 <-> node4 enp8s0 10.50.24.2/24), assigned OPT1/OPT2 in OPNsense, added firewall pass rules, added port-forward (DNAT) rules on both the transit (OPT1) and LAN (vtnet0, serving node3's lan-a) interfaces to node4:8080, and added a hairpin source-NAT rule so lan-a-originated traffic returns correctly through node2 despite node4 also sitting on the shared default network. Bound node4's demo HTTP service only to its lan-b address so it cannot be reached by addressing node4 directly. Verified node1 and node3 both reach the service via node2:80, while direct node4:8080 access from node3 fails. All config was persisted (VyOS config.boot save, OPNsense config.xml, NetworkManager profile, systemd service, firewalld permanent rule). Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all four nodes one at a time, confirming boot-identity changes via boot_id/kern.boottime and re-verifying service health, config persistence, and end-to-end reachability after each restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (VyOS, 3 NICs), node2 (OPNsense, 3 NICs), node3 (CentOS, 2 NICs), node4 (CentOS, 2 NICs) share a flat default network plus spare interfaces
Empirically determined via trial IP assignment + ping that node2 vtnet1 pairs with node1 eth1 (transit) and node2 vtnet2 pairs with node4 enp8s0 (lan-b)
Assigned OPNsense OPT1 (vtnet1, 10.50.12.1/24, transit) and OPT2 (vtnet2, 10.50.24.1/24, lan-b) via config.xml + configctl interface reconfigure
Removed erroneous blockpriv setting that was blocking private-source traffic on the new interfaces
Added OPNsense firewall pass rules for OPT1 and OPT2
Added NAT port-forward (DNAT) rules: OPT1:80 -> 10.50.24.2:8080 and vtnet0(LAN):80 -> 10.50.24.2:8080
Disabled OPNsense webConfigurator's automatic http->https redirect (disablehttpredirect) which was intercepting port 80 on LAN via the anti-lockout no-rdr rule

Added a hairpin outbound source-NAT rule (nat/outbound/rule) on OPT2 masquerading lan-a-sourced traffic destined to 10.50.24.2:8080, fixing asymmetric routing since node4 is also on the shared default network
Configured node1 eth1 as 10.50.12.2/24 via VyOS configure/commit/save, giving it a connected route to node2's transit address
Configured node4 enp8s0 as static 10.50.24.2/24 via nmcli, added a static route back to 10.50.12.0/24 via node2's lan-b address
Created and enabled a persistent systemd service on node4 serving HTTP on port 8080, bound only to 10.50.24.2 so it isn't reachable via node4's default-network address
Opened port 8080/tcp permanently in firewalld on node4
Verified end-to-end: node1 and node3 both reach the service via node2 port 80; direct node4:8080 access from node3 fails
Captured pre-restart health baselines (boot_id/kern.boottime, service status) on all four nodes
Restarted node1, then node2, then node3, then node4 one at a time via native reboot, polling until exec was available again
Confirmed changed boot identity on every node (boot_id changed on node1/node3/node4; kern.boottime changed on node2)
Re-verified config persistence and end-to-end service reachability after each individual restart

evidence.requirement: Service published on node4:8080, reachable via node2's transit address on port 80 from node1
evidence.summary: curl http://10.50.12.1:80/ from node1 returns HTTP 200 with body 'node4-service-ok', both before and after node1/node2/node4 restarts

evidence.requirement: node3 on lan-a reaches the service by asking node2 rather than addressing node4 directly
evidence.summary: curl http://10.100.231.11:80/ from node3 returns HTTP 200 via node2, while direct curl to node4's exposed address on 8080 times out (000), confirming segmentation is enforced by node2's forwarding

evidence.requirement: node1 given a working route to node2's transit address
evidence.summary: VyOS config.boot shows eth1 address 10.50.12.2/24 persisted; ip route on node1 shows connected route to 10.50.12.0/24 via eth1

evidence.requirement: OPNsense NAT/interface/firewall configuration correctly applied and persisted
evidence.summary: config.xml edits for OPT1/OPT2 interfaces, filter rules, DNAT rules and hairpin SNAT rule applied via configctl; pf ruleset shows rdr and nat rules present, and still present after node2 reboot

evidence.requirement: Baseline health capture before restarts on all 4 nodes
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (node1/node3/node4) and kern.boottime (node2) plus service/firewall health prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent exec timed out confirming outage; boot_id changed from 2674ee60... to d2dfc50d...; eth1 config and route to node2 confirmed present, service reachable post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state and quorum with dependents
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; kern.boottime changed from sec=1788670969 to sec=1788672019 confirming real restart; OPT1/OPT2 IPs and NAT rules persisted; both node1 and node3 paths to the service recovered post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 21de1f79... to 05be84f1...; enp1s0 IP restored via DHCP and curl to node2:80 returns 200 post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state (service, firewall, network, data path)
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 8f258838... to e0597c65...; static IP, systemd node4-http.service, and firewalld port 8080 rule all persisted and active post-reboot; end-to-end service access from node1 and node3 confirmed working, direct node4 access still blocked
